voice.text: An ice cream in the sun. [pause] A big oak tree. [pause] Which one is changing right now? Tap your guess.
Some changes are <emphasis>fast</emphasis>. [pause] A leaf falls. Ice cream melts. [pause] You can watch them happen!
Some changes are <emphasis>slow</emphasis>. [pause] A seed becomes a tree. A puppy becomes a dog. [pause] Too slow to watch — but they never stop changing.
Living things change by <emphasis>growing</emphasis>. [pause] Nonliving things get <emphasis>changed</emphasis> — waves wear the sandcastle down, [pause] and people build a road.
First, find each thing's after picture. [pause] Then tell me: was that change fast, or slow?
What does it become? [pause] Tap the after picture.
Was that change fast, [pause] or slow?
Yes! [pause] That is what it becomes.
Yes! [pause] You can watch that one happen. Fast!
Yes! [pause] Too slow to watch, but always changing. Slow!
Not quite. [pause] Think what it turns into after a while.
Not quite. [pause] You can't watch it move, but it is changing — a little every day. That is a slow change.
Not quite. [pause] You could stand and watch this one happen. That is a fast change.
All matched and sorted! [pause] Now show what you know.
A seed becomes a tall tree. Is the seed changing? [pause] Yes — slowly, even when we can't see it move, [pause] or, no — it isn't moving, so it isn't changing?
Which change is fast? [pause] Ice cream melting in the sun, [pause] or a puppy growing into a dog?
Waves wash the sandcastle flat. Can a nonliving sandcastle change? [pause] Yes — the waves change it, [pause] or, no — only living things change?
How does a puppy become a dog? [pause] It grows a little every day, [pause] or it changes all at once, in one night?
Which change is slow? [pause] A seed growing into a tree, [pause] or a leaf falling from the branch?
<soft>You can spot changes, fast and slow!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the changes once more.
Lesson done! Pick one thing to watch change this month. A plant, or the moon. Draw it in your journal every few days.
